title: House Money
subtitle: A Card Room on the Strip, Three Thousand Acres, a Buick with No Brakes

setting.name: Los Angeles and the West Valley, Saturday 27 to Tuesday 30 September 1947
setting.description: Four days of following money. The negatives show two councilmen taking envelopes at a card table; this scenario is about whose money it was, what it was buying and who died when the money was refused. The party works the Sunset Strip and Club Sirocco, where Royce Ambler runs the card room and has started to panic; the Hall of Records and City Hall downtown, where shell companies and water-main plans leave paper; the Pacific Electric line over the hills to Van Nuys; a wrecking yard on Sepulveda Boulevard where a dead councilman's Buick is rusting; and the West Valley orange groves, where Wendell Haig's survey stakes run through the grove the Okada family planted in 1921 and lost in 1942. On Saturday, Harlan Shay, frightened after the vault, tells Haig the ledger is missing, and Haig sends for the man who took care of Councilman Mabry.
setting.atmosphere: Two worlds and the money that runs between them. The Sirocco on a Saturday night: a twelve-piece band, white dinner jackets, a ceiling painted with desert stars, the click of chips upstairs and a two-way mirror. The Hall of Records: dust, ledgers, clerks with green eyeshades, the slow thrill of finding a name in a filing. Then over the Cahuenga Pass into the Valley: miles of dark orange groves in straight rows, the smell of blossom and irrigation water and eucalyptus, packing sheds, chicken ranches, a sky full of stars, and red-flagged survey stakes marching through the trees where nobody has voted to put a road. The violence escalates in this scenario: Wendell Haig's men burn things, and Emory Thorne kills people. Keep the city's greed concrete: the $300 acre that becomes a $3,000 acre, the veterans who need houses, the family who planted the trees.

keyLocations.name: Club Sirocco: the Palm Court, the Card Room and Ambler's Office
keyLocations.description: Upstairs at the Sirocco, behind a door with no handle off the service corridor: a card room with four tables under green-shaded lamps, a bar, a cashier's cage where Lew Pardee keeps the chips and the books, and along one wall a long gilt mirror that is glass on one side and a window on the other, behind which Ambler's photographer, a nervous man named Ozzie Feld, sits with a Speed Graphic on a tripod. Ambler's office is next door, with the safe behind a painting of a camel.
features: The palm court and dance floor: a public place where nobody can be shot without three hundred witnesses
The card room, the two-way mirror and the photographer's closet behind it
Lew Pardee's cashier's cage and its daybook of chips in and out
Ambler's office: the safe (combination 4-17-98, the same as before; he changed it to 9-14-47 the day after the theft), a private stair to the alley
encounters: Royce Ambler, sweating through a white dinner jacket, who wants to deal
Tiny Bascombe (Bouncer) and two Bouncers on the door; two Sheriff's deputies at the bar who are on Ambler's payroll (Crooked Cops)
Lew Pardee, card-room cashier, sixty, a bookkeeper who used to keep honest books
On Saturday night, at the card table: Councilman Dwight Hollister losing on purpose to someone, or winning on purpose
secrets: CLUE M1d (core, Lew Pardee, if the party gets him alone and promises him protection, or Persuasion DC 13): 'The councilmen win. They always win. Mr. Ambler sets the table, the studio's money buys the chips, and the councilmen cash out. Five thousand a night for Hollister, five for Fenwick, every second Saturday since March. It comes in from a company called Cahuenga Location Services. I've got the daybook.' His daybook is the cash side of the green ledger.

CLUE M3d (core, Pardee again, or Ambler when he deals): 'Mabry wouldn't sit down. He came up here once, in August, looked at the table and walked out. Then Haig brought in a man from Chicago, an insurance adjuster, Mr. Ambler said. Quiet man. Never took his hat off.'
Ozzie Feld, the photographer, has prints of everything at his darkroom on Fountain Avenue. He is terrified, and Thorne will kill him on Monday night unless the party gets to him first.

Ambler's deal (offered through Percy, or in person on Sunday): he will give the party the daybook, the photographer, and his testimony about Haig, in exchange for the green ledger back (which protects him) and their protection until the vote. He means about half of it.

keyLocations.name: The Hall of Records and City Hall
keyLocations.description: Downtown, a block apart. The Hall of Records: the County Recorder's deed books, the corporation filings copied from Sacramento, and a reading room with long oak tables and a clerk who has worked there since 1911. City Hall: the twenty-eight-storey white tower, the council chamber with its gold ceiling, the city clerk's office with the agendas, and on the ninth floor the engineering office of the water department, where plans are drawn on linen and filed in long flat drawers.
features: The corporation index and the deed books, which take hours to search and reward patience
The council agenda for Tuesday 7 October, Item 14: 'Annexation of the West Valley Tract and extension of water service'
The engineering plan room and its filing cabinets of drawings, each dated and initialled
encounters: Miss Hortense Gale, recorder's clerk since 1911, who loves a researcher who knows what they want
Mr. Leon Szabo, junior engineer, twenty-nine, a veteran with a conscience and a mortgage
Councilman Dwight Hollister, if the party goes to his office: genial, red-faced, outraged, and on the telephone to Haig within ten minutes (+1 Heat)
secrets: CLUE M1b (core, Research in the corporation index, DC 10 for speed): Cahuenga Location Services, Inc., incorporated February 1947; directors Mortimer Gaines (attorney, Sunset Boulevard) and R. Ambler. With Agnes Whitlow's or Percy's access to the studio's location accounts (or Research DC 15 at the studio's bank), Castellane Pictures has paid it $180,000 since March for 'location rental, Western unit', and the Western unit shot every one of its pictures this year on the studio's own movie ranch, which Cotton Ridley will confirm.

CLUE M2b (core, the deed books, Research DC 12 for the full picture): Encino Verde Land Co. has bought three thousand acres in the West Valley since 1942, mostly at $200 to $350 an acre, including forty acres on Reseda Road bought in May 1942 from 'S. Okada' for $1,600 through a straw buyer. Encino Verde's 1946 annual statement lists its president, Wendell Haig, and its directors, among them 'B. Castellane'.

CLUE M2c (core, Leon Szabo or the plan drawers, Investigation DC 13 if the party searches without him): plans for a twenty-four-inch water main from Reseda Boulevard west to the Encino Verde lands, drawn in June 1947, three months before the annexation was put on any agenda, marked in pencil 'expedite per Mr. Haig / approved D.H.'. Szabo will say so to a reporter or a grand jury if the party keeps his name out of it until then.

Red herring: the annexation is popular. Veterans' groups support it, the newspapers support it, and the houses will be real houses for real families. Haig is not wrong that the city needs them. He is a crook because of how, not what.

keyLocations.name: The Okada Grove, Reseda Road
keyLocations.description: Forty acres of Valencia oranges planted in 1921 by Shigeru and Haru Okada, with a packing shed, a windmill, a small frame house and an irrigation reservoir the size of a living room. Sold under duress in May 1942 when the family was sent to Manzanar; the family returned in 1945 and now works the grove as Encino Verde's tenant managers, for wages, on trees they planted. Shigeru is sixty-eight. His daughter, Amy Okada, thirty, kept the farm's books before the war and keeps them now. Ken Hirano is Shigeru's nephew.
features: The rows: dark, sweet-smelling, straight, cool even in the afternoon, fine cover and terrible for seeing more than a row away
Red-flagged survey stakes running diagonally through the grove, across the irrigation furrows
The packing shed: crates, a grading belt, a truck, and the family's records in a tin trunk
The irrigation night: water runs in the furrows on Monday nights, turning the rows to mud
encounters: Amy Okada, who does not trust anyone from the city and has excellent reasons; she trusts Ken, and she trusts people who listen
Shigeru Okada, who will show the party the tree he planted the day Amy was born, and nothing else until Amy says so

On Monday night: Haig's men come to burn the packing shed, because the Okadas have been talking to people (two Hired Guns with Molotov cocktails, a Getaway Driver in a stake truck, and Haig's foreman, Clete Varney, a Mob Torpedo)
secrets: CLUE M2a (core, the stakes and Amy): Haig's surveyors came through in July, before any vote was scheduled, and staked the line for a water main and a road, and a man from Encino Verde told Amy that 'the city will be out here by Christmas'. She has the surveyor's card: 'Valley Engineering, for Encino Verde Land Co., per W. Haig'. In the tin trunk: the 1942 bill of sale for $1,600, and a letter from the straw buyer saying he was acting 'for a client'.

CLUE M3a support (Amy): Councilman Arthur Mabry came to the grove on 26 August, alone, asked to see the stakes and the bill of sale, and said, 'Miss Okada, I think I'm going to make some people very unhappy.' Four days later he was dead.
Ken Hirano's player knows this family. The GM should give Ken the first scene here, and let Amy and Shigeru speak to him before anyone else.
If the packing shed burns, the family's records burn with it unless someone saves the tin trunk. Saving it is an action in the fire (Athletics DC 12, 2d6 fire damage on a failure).

keyLocations.name: The Red Car to Van Nuys and Swede Lindgren's Wrecking Yard
keyLocations.description: The Pacific Electric's Valley line runs from the Hollywood stops through the Cahuenga Pass to North Hollywood and Van Nuys, big red cars with a clanging bell and wicker seats, and from the Van Nuys station it is a walk down Sepulveda Boulevard to a wrecking yard behind a corrugated fence: five acres of dead cars stacked three high, a crane, a shack, two Guard Dogs and Swede Lindgren, seventy, who buys what the insurance companies write off.
features: The Red Car: thirty passengers, a motorman, a conductor, wicker seats, open windows, a rear platform and a long grade through the pass
The yard's rows of wrecks, the crane with its electromagnet, the shack with a ledger of every car in
Mabry's 1946 Buick Roadmaster in row G, roof crushed, front end folded, waiting to be crushed itself on Wednesday
encounters: On the Red Car: Haig's men, or Thorne himself, riding three seats behind the party (Perception DC 15 to notice a quiet man in a grey hat who never looks out of the window)
Swede Lindgren, who will let the party look at anything for $5 and sell them anything for $20
Two Guard Dogs, loose after dark
secrets: CLUE M3b (core, anyone who looks at the brakes with Mechanics, or anyone at all if Swede shows them): the Buick's front brake line has been cut most of the way through with a fine saw, cleanly, at a place where it would hold for a few miles and fail on the first long downhill. Mulholland Drive is all long downhills. Swede: 'Insurance man looked at it and wrote it off. I seen sawn lines before. This one, somebody knew what he was doing.'

The insurance adjuster who wrote off the Buick and ruled out mechanical tampering, according to Swede's ledger, was 'E. Thomas, Midwest Indemnity'. There is no such company. It was Thorne, closing his own case.
If the party does not come by Tuesday, the Buick is crushed on Wednesday morning. Swede can be paid $20 to wait.

keyLocations.name: Mrs. Helen Mabry's House, Los Feliz
keyLocations.description: A Spanish-style house on a hillside street in Los Feliz, with the curtains drawn, a black wreath still on the door, a dog that waits by the front window, and a desk in the study where Councilman Mabry worked at night.
features: The study: Mabry's appointment diary, his files, a city map with the West Valley Tract outlined in red pencil
The garage, where the Buick was serviced the week before he died
encounters: Helen Mabry, fifty-two, a former schoolteacher, who has been told by everyone that it was an accident and has never believed it
secrets: CLUE M3a (core, a respectful visit): 'Arthur said someone had offered him money to vote for the Valley annexation. A great deal of money. He said no and he said he was going to find out where it came from. He drove up to the Valley twice. The car was serviced the Tuesday before at our garage on Vermont and they said the brakes were perfect. He drove Mulholland every night of his life; he said it was the only place he could think.' His diary for 30 August: '9 p.m. Mulholland lookout, re: W.H. (will he come himself?)'.
Mabry's file on the West Valley Tract, in his desk: notes on Encino Verde, the Okada bill of sale, and the words 'Who is B.C.?' underlined twice.
Mrs. Mabry wants the truth told publicly. If the party promises her that, she will stand beside them at the end.

keyLocations.name: The Carousel Horse and the Green Ledger
keyLocations.description: When the party has earned it (by finding the negatives and keeping faith with her), Vivian takes them back to the Santa Monica pier after closing, climbs onto the outside-row black horse with the gold mane, unscrews its saddle and takes out a green cloth-bound ledger.
features: The ledger: a hundred pages of Royce Ambler's neat Kansas City accounting, in initials and figures, March to September 1947
encounters: Mags Fennimore, who insists on holding the flashlight and on being told everything
secrets: CLUE M1c (core, reading it): every second Saturday, 'D.H. 5,000; R.F. 5,000; H.S. host; via CLS'. And the receipts from Cahuenga Location Services, $180,000 in all.
CLUE M2d (core): a page headed 'E.V. partners', with 'W.H. 60%, B.C. 40%', and beside it, 'B.C. pays through the studio, H.S. carries'.
CLUE M3c (core): 'Aug. 27. A.M. refused. Referred to E.T., Chicago. $2,500 + exp. Aug. 31. Settled.'
The ledger also shows Harlan Shay as 'host' at every payment. It does not show he knew about Mabry, and he did not.

synopsis: The negatives prove two councilmen took envelopes at a card table on the Sunset Strip. This scenario is about whose money it was, what it bought, and who paid for refusing it. At Club Sirocco, Royce Ambler, who has just learned that Wendell Haig knows the ledger is gone, is sweating through his dinner jacket and wants to sell Haig to the party for protection; his card-room cashier, Lew Pardee, explains how the councilmen are allowed to win. At the Hall of Records the money becomes paper: $180,000 in studio 'location fees' to a shell called Cahuenga Location Services, owned by Ambler, and three thousand acres of West Valley groves held by Encino Verde Land Co., whose directors include Bernard Castellane, head of the studio. At City Hall a young engineer has plans for a water main to Haig's land drawn three months before anyone voted on it. In the Valley, the grove the Okada family planted in 1921 has survey stakes running through it, Councilman Arthur Mabry came asking about it four days before his brakes failed on Mulholland, and a wrecking yard on Sepulveda has his Buick, with its brake line sawn. Vivian finally takes the party to the carousel horse where she hid the green ledger, and it names everyone, including a professional from Chicago, 'E.T.', paid $2,500 to settle Mabry. Haig's men try to burn the Okadas' packing shed; Emory Thorne begins cleaning up Haig's loose ends, starting with the photographer and then Ambler. The scenario ends on Tuesday night with Ambler dead or saved, Thorne's name known, and the studio announcing that Vivian Lark will attend her premiere on Saturday, because Vivian has telephoned Harlan Shay and told him so.
hook: Saturday night, and the Sirocco is full. The band is playing something with a rumba in it and four hundred people are pretending not to look at each other, and Percy Ainsworth's table by the dance floor is the best in the house because Royce Ambler sent a bottle of champagne to it before Percy sat down. With the champagne is a card in Ambler's neat hand: 'I believe we have mutual friends and a mutual problem. My office, midnight. Bring anyone you trust. R.A.' Upstairs, behind a door with no handle, chips are clicking. On the dance floor a red-faced man with a councilman's lapel pin is dancing very badly with a contract player from Castellane who is smiling as if she has been paid to, which she has.

conclusions.conclusion: Castellane studio money is buying Councilmen Hollister and Fenwick through the Sirocco card room.
clues: M1a: The negatives from can 14: the councilmen taking envelopes at the card table (from kl-scenario-002)
M1b: Cahuenga Location Services, Ambler's shell, paid $180,000 by the studio for locations never used (Hall of Records, studio accounts, Cotton Ridley)
M1c: The green ledger's every-second-Saturday entries (the carousel horse)
M1d: Lew Pardee and his daybook (Club Sirocco)

conclusions.conclusion: The money is buying Wendell Haig's West Valley annexation and water mains, voted on 7 October, and Bernard Castellane is Haig's silent forty per cent partner.
clues: M2a: The survey stakes through the Okada grove in July, and Amy Okada's 1942 bill of sale and surveyor's card (the West Valley)
M2b: Encino Verde Land Co.'s deeds and its 1946 statement listing B. Castellane as a director (Hall of Records)
M2c: The water-main plans drawn in June, 'expedite per Mr. Haig / approved D.H.' (City Hall, Leon Szabo)
M2d: The ledger's 'E.V. partners' page (the carousel horse)

conclusions.conclusion: Councilman Arthur Mabry was murdered for refusing the money, by a professional Haig brought from Chicago: Emory Thorne.
clues: M3a: Helen Mabry: the refused bribe, the perfect brakes, the diary entry for 30 August (Los Feliz)
M3b: The sawn brake line in Swede Lindgren's yard, and the 'insurance adjuster' E. Thomas who wrote it off (Van Nuys)
M3c: The ledger: 'A.M. refused. Referred to E.T., Chicago. $2,500' (the carousel horse)
M3d: Lew Pardee: Haig's 'insurance adjuster from Chicago' who never took off his hat (Club Sirocco)

M3e: Ken Hirano drove 'a man from Chicago' for Shay from the Burbank air terminal to the Casa Ventura Motor Court on 29 August, and to the Mulholland lookout on the 30th 'to see the view'; or the motor court register: 'E. Thorne, Chicago, Aug. 29 to 31, transport by Castellane studio' (Ventura Boulevard)

acts.title: Act 1: The Card Room
acts.description: Saturday 27 and Sunday 28 September. The Sirocco, Ambler's offer, and the men who win at cards. Ambler knows by Saturday evening that Haig knows; Shay told Haig after the vault. Ambler is frightened enough to deal and arrogant enough to think he can still win.
objectives: Meet Ambler at midnight and hear his offer
See the card room, the two-way mirror and the photographer
Get Lew Pardee and his daybook
Decide whether to protect Ambler, use him, or let him hang

scenes.name: Midnight, Upstairs
scenes.description: Ambler's office, with Tiny at the door and a painting of a camel over the safe. Ambler pours good bourbon and talks fast. He wants the green ledger back, the party's protection until the vote, and in exchange offers Pardee's daybook, Ozzie Feld's prints, and his own testimony against Haig 'when the time is right'.
scenes.readAloud: Ambler's office is small and expensive and smells of cigars and fear. He is a lean man with grey at his temples and the long, careful hands of a card dealer, and he pours four fingers of bourbon into each glass without spilling a drop, but his collar is wet. Behind him a painting of a camel in a gilt frame stares out at nothing. 'Let me tell you about Wendell Haig,' he says. 'Wendell Haig is a man who wants something very badly, and when Wendell Haig wants something, things that are in the way stop being in the way. I've been something he wanted for six months. Since Saturday, I'm something in the way.'

skillChecks.success: Ambler is telling the truth about being afraid of Haig and lying about what he will do with the ledger: he wants it to sell back to Haig for his life. He does not know the name of Haig's man from Chicago, only that he exists.
skillChecks.failure: Ambler sounds sincere. He is a professional gambler; sounding sincere is his trade.

skillChecks.success: Ambler hands over Pardee's daybook tonight as a down payment, without getting the ledger first.
skillChecks.failure: Ambler wants the ledger in his hand before he gives anything. He gives the party until Tuesday.

scenes.name: Behind the Mirror
scenes.description: The card room on a Saturday night, and the closet behind the two-way mirror where Ozzie Feld sits with his camera. A good place for a Grifter's long con, a Fixer's favour or a Heavy's quiet word.
scenes.readAloud: Through the glass the card room is a painting: four tables under green lamps, men in dinner jackets, chips in towers, smoke rising straight up in the still air like strings holding the ceiling up. At the second table Councilman Dwight Hollister rakes in a pot with both arms and laughs, and the man across from him, who has just lost on purpose, laughs too. In the closet beside you a thin man with a Speed Graphic changes a film holder with shaking hands and whispers, without looking round, 'If Mr. Ambler sent you, tell him I've done the roll, and if he didn't, God help me.'

skillChecks.success: Ozzie Feld gives you the address of his darkroom on Fountain Avenue and begs for protection. He has prints of everything.
skillChecks.failure: Ozzie panics and calls for Tiny. Leave quickly or fight in a closet.

skillChecks.success: Lew Pardee's daybook leaves the cashier's cage in someone's coat. (Or ask Pardee: M1d is core if he is asked privately and promised protection.)
skillChecks.failure: Pardee sees and says nothing, which tells you he wants to be caught.

encounters: Tiny Bascombe and two Bouncers; two Sheriff's deputies on Ambler's payroll (Crooked Cops) at the bar; fighting in the club brings the Sheriff's vice squad in four minutes (+3 Heat for gunfire, and Ambler's deputies are on Ambler's side)
A Knife Artist among the card room's regulars, a dealer named Felix who works for Ambler when there is trouble

acts.title: Act 2: Paper
acts.description: Monday 29 September. Downtown and the Valley. The Hall of Records, City Hall, Helen Mabry, the Red Car to Van Nuys and the wrecking yard, the Okada grove. Each place gives a piece of M1, M2 or M3. Vivian, if the party has kept faith, takes them to the carousel horse for the ledger. Thorne is working too: by Monday night he has killed Ozzie Feld in his darkroom, unless the party got to him first.
objectives: Find Cahuenga Location Services and Encino Verde on paper
Get the water-main plans and Leon Szabo
See Mabry's Buick before it is crushed
Go to the Okada grove; let Ken Hirano lead
Get the green ledger from Vivian

scenes.name: The Reading Room
scenes.description: The Hall of Records. Run a research montage: let the players say what they are looking for and give it to them, with Miss Gale's help, at the cost of time. A Research check sets how many hours it takes (DC 10: two hours; DC 15: one; failure: four, and someone sees them).
scenes.readAloud: The reading room is long and high and brown, with oak tables, green lamps, and tall windows through which the afternoon comes in slanted and full of dust. A clerk in a lace collar who has been here since 1911 brings you the deed books one at a time on a trolley, each one as heavy as a paving stone, and says, 'If you tell me what you're looking for, dear, I'll tell you which book it's in. If you don't, we'll both be here till Christmas.'

skillChecks.success: M1b and M2b in two hours: Cahuenga Location Services and its directors; Encino Verde's three thousand acres, the Okada deed and the directors' list with B. Castellane on it.
skillChecks.failure: Four hours, and a clerk who works for Councilman Hollister's office notices what you're asking for. +1 Heat, and Haig knows the party has been in the deed books.

scenes.name: The Valley Line
scenes.description: The Red Car over the Cahuenga Pass to Van Nuys, and the walk to Swede's yard. A good scene for a tail: Thorne, or two of Haig's men, are on the car. A fight on a moving Red Car is a fight on difficult terrain with thirty terrified passengers, a motorman who will stop the car at the next station and call the police, and a long drop from the rear platform.
scenes.readAloud: The big red car sways and clangs up through the pass, wicker seats creaking, windows open on dry hills and the smell of sage and hot brake shoes. A sailor sleeps against the window. Two women argue about a hat. The conductor calls the stops in a singsong, North Hollywood, Lankershim, and the Valley opens out below you flat and green and gold to the far mountains, orange groves in rows to the edge of the world. Three seats behind you a man in a grey hat reads nothing and has not looked out of the window once.

skillChecks.success: You see the man in the grey hat, and you see him see you see him. He gets off at North Hollywood without hurry. That was Emory Thorne, and now you have a face.
skillChecks.failure: You do not notice him. Swede Lindgren later mentions 'another fella came asking about the Buick an hour before you, grey hat, wanted to know when it was getting crushed'.

skillChecks.success: On the Buick: the brake line was sawn through three-quarters with a fine jeweller's saw, from underneath, by someone who has done it before. (M3b is core if anyone looks; this adds that it was done with the car on a jack, at night, in a garage, which means at the Mabrys' own garage on the night of the 29th.)
skillChecks.failure: The line is cut (core). You cannot say more without Bunny or Cotton Ridley.

scenes.name: Forty Acres
scenes.description: The Okada grove. Ken Hirano's scene first. Amy Okada's records, the survey stakes, Mabry's visit. Shigeru shows the party the tree he planted the day Amy was born.
scenes.readAloud: The grove is so quiet that you can hear the windmill turning at the far end of it, and the water running in the furrows. The trees are dark and glossy and heavy with green fruit, in rows so straight that looking down one is like looking down a corridor in a dream. Through them, diagonally, cutting across the rows as if the trees were not there, runs a line of wooden stakes with red rags tied to their tops, one every hundred feet, as far as you can see. A small, upright old man in a straw hat is standing by one of them with a pair of pruning shears, looking at it.

skillChecks.success: Amy Okada has been waiting five years for someone from the city to ask her what happened. She will tell you everything if you let her tell it her own way, from 1942.
skillChecks.failure: Amy gives you the facts (core) and nothing else. She has learned what city people do with stories.

skillChecks.success: Shigeru Okada agrees to give a statement about the 1942 sale to a lawyer or a newspaper, under his own name. He has not done so before because no one asked who would listen.
skillChecks.failure: Shigeru says it is his daughter's decision. It is.

encounters: Thorne on the Red Car (use The Professional; he will not fight here unless cornered, and leaves)
Two Guard Dogs at the wrecking yard after dark

At Ozzie Feld's darkroom on Monday evening: Ozzie dead in his developing tank, and the prints gone, unless the party got there before 7 p.m. (+2 Heat when the body is found, and Dolan calls the party in)

acts.title: Act 3: Irrigation Night
acts.description: Monday night 29 September to Tuesday night 30 September. Haig strikes back. On Monday night his men come to burn the Okadas' packing shed and the records in it. On Tuesday night, Ambler, who has the party's promise or doesn't, goes to meet them, or to meet Haig, and Thorne is waiting. And at some point on Tuesday Vivian telephones Harlan Shay and tells him she will be at her premiere on Saturday. The scenario ends with the studio's announcement in Thursday's papers.
objectives: Defend the Okada packing shed and the tin trunk
Take one of Haig's men alive, or follow the truck back to Haig
Protect Ambler, or decide not to
Learn Emory Thorne's name and face
Talk Vivian out of the premiere, or into a plan

scenes.name: The Packing Shed
scenes.description: Monday, after ten. The water is running in the furrows and the rows are mud. A stake truck with no lights comes down the grove road. Clete Varney, Haig's foreman, and two Hired Guns with Molotov cocktails and pump shotguns. They want the shed burned and nobody seen; they will shoot if anyone tries to stop them.
scenes.readAloud: The irrigation water is running down every furrow in the grove, black and silver in the starlight, and the rows have gone to mud that sucks at your shoes. The windmill creaks. Then, from the grove road, there is the sound of an engine in low gear with no lights, and the smell of gasoline on the night air, and a man's voice saying, very quietly, 'The shed, and the house if it catches. Nobody hurt if they stay inside.'

skillChecks.success: Group check. The party moves down the rows in the dark and the mud without being seen. They have surprise.
skillChecks.failure: Someone slips in a furrow with a splash. Varney's men open up with a shotgun into the rows; the party is not surprised but neither are they.

skillChecks.success: If the shed catches: into the smoke, out with the tin trunk and the Okadas' records.
skillChecks.failure: Out with the tin trunk and 2d6 fire damage.

skillChecks.success: A captured Hired Gun talks: Varney hired them, Varney works for Haig, and Haig's 'insurance man' Mr. Thorne is staying at the Hotel Cordova on Hollywood Boulevard under the name E. Thomas.
skillChecks.failure: He wants a lawyer. Varney, if taken, says nothing and smiles.

scenes.name: Ambler's Last Hand
scenes.description: Tuesday night. Ambler goes to the meeting he arranged: with the party at the Castellane movie ranch (Cotton Ridley's ground), or, if the party refused him, with Haig at the Mulholland lookout to sell the party out. Thorne is there either way, with a hunting rifle, at three hundred yards. If the party has a watcher on the high ground and a plan, they can save Ambler (Perception DC 15 to spot the rifle's glint; Stealth to close on Thorne, who leaves the moment the shot is spoiled). If not, Ambler dies on his feet in his headlights.
scenes.readAloud: The Western street at the movie ranch has a saloon, a bank, a jail and a church, all fronts, all two-dimensional against the rocks in the moonlight, and Royce Ambler is standing in the middle of it in his white dinner jacket beside his Cadillac with its headlights on, like the last scene of a picture he would never have been allowed to make. He lights a cigarette. The match flares. 'Well,' he calls, 'I came, didn't I? Let's do business.'

skillChecks.success: On the ridge above the false-front church, three hundred yards off, a glint where there should be nothing. Shout, shoot, or tackle: Ambler lives if someone acts this round.
skillChecks.failure: A flat crack from the ridge. Ambler sits down in the dust beside his car as if he is very tired. By the time anyone reaches the ridge there is only a brass shell case, a .30-06, and tyre tracks.

skillChecks.success: Bunny or Cotton gets a car up the ranch road after Thorne's and sees the plate: a rented Ford, from a Burbank garage, rented to E. Thomas.
skillChecks.failure: Thorne's car is gone into the hills without lights.

scenes.name: Vivian's Decision
scenes.description: Tuesday, late. Vivian has the ledger back (or the party has it), knows about Mabry, Kurland and now Ambler, and has made a decision: she has called Shay and told him she will attend her own premiere on Saturday. The studio will announce it on Thursday. She intends to walk up to the radio microphone in front of the Pantheon and read the ledger into it. Let the party argue. She will not be talked out of going, but she will listen to a plan.
scenes.readAloud: 'Abel wanted to do it quietly,' Vivian says. 'Quietly got him drowned. Mr. Mabry did it quietly and they cut his brakes.' She is sitting on the floor of Mags's apartment with her back against the wall and the green ledger in her lap, and the foghorn is going outside. 'On Saturday night every newspaper in Los Angeles will be on Hollywood Boulevard, and KHLW will have a microphone on the forecourt, and every one of those men will be in the front rows in a dinner jacket. Harlan says I'm to wear the silver gown. I'm going to wear it.' She looks up. 'So. Are you going to help me, or am I going to do it without you?'

skillChecks.success: Vivian agrees to a plan the party makes: who carries the ledger, who watches the roof, when she speaks, and what she does if the party says stop. She will follow it.
skillChecks.failure: Vivian agrees to let the party come. She does not agree to anything else.

encounters: Clete Varney (Mob Torpedo), two Hired Guns with pump shotguns and two Molotov cocktails each, and a Getaway Driver in a stake truck, at the Okada grove
Emory Thorne (The Professional) with a hunting rifle on the ridge at the movie ranch; he does not close to melee, and he leaves when the shot is spoiled or a second shooter finds him
Haig's men at the Mulholland lookout (a Hired Gun and a Getaway Driver) if Ambler goes to sell the party out instead

npcsInvolved.name: Wendell Haig, 58
npcsInvolved.role: President of Encino Verde Land Co. and Haig Homesites; the man behind it all
npcsInvolved.description: Big, pink-faced, sixty, a ring with a blue stone, a booming laugh, a Rotary pin, and photographs of himself with veterans' groups on every wall. He believes he is building the future of Los Angeles, and he may be right about the houses. He fights through other men and has never fired a gun in his life.
npcsInvolved.motivation: The vote on 7 October. Three thousand acres at ten times their price. He will pay anyone, buy anyone, and have anyone in the way removed, and sleep well.

npcsInvolved.name: Royce Ambler, 49
npcsInvolved.role: Owner of Club Sirocco; the bookkeeper of the bribes
npcsInvolved.description: Lean, grey at the temples, a card dealer's hands, Kansas City accent, sweating through a white dinner jacket. Courteous to the end.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Live. Get the ledger back and sell it to Haig for his life, or sell Haig to the party for theirs. Dies on Tuesday night unless the party saves him; if saved, he testifies, with a great deal of complaining.

npcsInvolved.name: Emory Thorne, 45
npcsInvolved.role: The professional from Chicago; Mabry's killer
npcsInvolved.description: Medium height, grey suit, grey hat he never takes off indoors, a face nobody remembers, a voice like a bank manager. Travels as E. Thomas, insurance adjuster. Never in a hurry. Uses a fine saw, a hunting rifle and other people's assumptions.
npcsInvolved.motivation: The job, and the fee. Haig has paid him $10,000 to recover the ledger and close the loose ends: the photographer, Ambler, the girl. He does not do anything for any other reason.

npcsInvolved.name: Lew Pardee, 60
npcsInvolved.description: A bookkeeper who once kept honest books for a Glendale lumber company, lost his job in 1932 and has been keeping dishonest ones since. Small, neat, sleeve garters, a daughter in Fresno he sends money to.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To be caught by someone who will keep him alive.

npcsInvolved.name: Amy Okada, 30, and Shigeru Okada, 68
npcsInvolved.role: The family who planted the grove; Ken Hirano's cousin and uncle
npcsInvolved.description: Amy kept the farm's books before the war, kept a ledger in the camp, and keeps one now. Precise, wary, dry-humoured. Shigeru planted the trees in 1921 and works them for wages now; he speaks little and misses nothing.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To get the land back, and failing that, to have it said in public how it was taken.

npcsInvolved.name: Helen Mabry, 52
npcsInvolved.description: A former schoolteacher with a schoolteacher's spine. Has been patted on the hand by everyone in City Hall for a month and is finished with it.

npcsInvolved.name: Leon Szabo, 29
npcsInvolved.description: An Army engineer in the war, a new house in Burbank, a baby. He drew the plans and has been sick about it since June.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To do the right thing without losing the house.

npcsInvolved.name: Cotton Ridley
npcsInvolved.role: Caretaker of the Castellane movie ranch; companion
npcsInvolved.description: Full sheet in the companion files. He knows the Western unit never shot a frame anywhere but his ranch, and he knows the Valley.
npcsInvolved.motivation: The studio's been paying for locations it never used, and he's been sweeping the same Western street for nine years. He wants to know where the money went.

rewards.money: Shay's money has stopped by now unless the party is still reporting to him. Ambler, if saved, pays $500 'for my life, which I value at slightly more than that'. Varney's men carry $80. The Okadas offer nothing and a crate of Valencias, which is the better reward.
items: The green ledger (clues M1c, M2d, M3c)
Lew Pardee's daybook, and Pardee himself as a witness
Ozzie Feld's prints, if the party reached his darkroom before Thorne
Copies of the Encino Verde deeds and directors' list, and Leon Szabo's water-main plans
The Okadas' tin trunk: the 1942 bill of sale and the straw buyer's letter
A pump shotgun and Shotgun shells (10) from Varney's men, if beaten
Emory Thorne's alias, hotel and face

twists: Bernard Castellane, the head of the studio that hired the party, is Haig's partner. The studio is not a victim of the scheme; it is paying for it, because without the Valley money it will be bankrupt by spring.

Harlan Shay arranged Emory Thorne's car from the airport as a favour to Haig, and Ken Hirano drove it. Shay has suspected since 31 August what Thorne was for and has never let himself know it. Ken's player knows something they did not know they knew.

The annexation is a good idea done crookedly. Veterans need houses; the city needs to grow. The players may find themselves wanting the houses built and the crooks jailed, and those may not both be possible.
Ambler, the most obviously crooked man in the case, becomes the most useful witness if the party keeps him alive, and he will complain about it every minute.

Vivian does not ask permission. Her decision to attend the premiere is hers, and it is the right one for her. The party's job in kl-scenario-004 is to keep her alive while she does it, or to change her mind, and she has earned the right to say no.
dmTips: This is the follow-the-money scenario, and it can bog down. Keep each piece of paper short, concrete and dramatic: a name in a deed book, a date on a plan, a dollar figure. Run the research as a montage with a cost in hours, not a series of rolls.
The three conclusions each have four or more clues. The party does not need all of them. When they have three for a conclusion, tell them plainly that it's solid, and move on.

Ken Hirano's scene at the grove is the heart of this scenario. If Ken is not in the party, Cotton Ridley knows the Okadas and makes the introduction. Treat the family as people, not as a lesson: Amy is funny and sharp and tired of explaining.

Emory Thorne should be seen before he acts: on the Red Car, in a hotel lobby, at the grove's edge at dusk. Then he acts, and the party knows what he looks like. He is a CR 5 professional and should not die in this scenario unless the party is very good; if they kill or capture him, kl-scenario-004's sniper becomes Clete Varney with a rifle (use Hit Man) and the shot is easier to stop.

Heat rises fast here: a fire, gunfire in the Valley, a body at the movie ranch, leaning on a councilman. At Heat 6, Dolan's men and Haig's men are both looking for the party; let them feel it, then give them Mrs. Mabry's spare room or Dr. Pryor's clinic to breathe.
Level-up note: the 3800 XP in this file is per character and takes each character from 4th to 5th level. Award it after Ambler's last hand, whatever its outcome.

Period texture: a rumba band at the Sirocco, white dinner jackets, the Red Car's bell in the pass, the scent of orange groves at night, the windmill, survey stakes with red rags, a newspaper photograph of Councilman Hollister cutting a ribbon at a veterans' housing tract, the World Series on the radio.
